newsitem.title: FRANCE: ABN Amro chief sees no good banks to buy.
newsitem.headline: ABN Amro chief sees no good banks to buy.

text.p: Jan Kalff, managing board chairman of acquisition-hungry Dutch bank ABN Amro, said in a newspaper interview on Friday none of Europe's good banks were for sale and nothing had come of French banks it had looked at.
"It has to be said the none of the good banks in Europe are for sale and all the candidates have problems," Kalff said in an interview in financial daily Les Echos.
"Paribas approached us on Credit du Nord, we looked at CIC and even looked at Credit Lyonnais but all that came to nothing," he was quoted as saying.
"Eastern Europe? -- too far...Germany is a hurdle between us and eastern Europe," he said.
He highlighted his bank's interest in the United States.

"Americans are less attached to the name of their bank than Europeans and we always give the institutions which we buy the name of our own main bank in the marketplace, the marketplace name that is, not that of ABN Amro," he said.
"In France NSM is well known and has a good reputation. I'm not convinced that we have anything to gain from changing it."
Kalff said ABN Amro was present in 10 states of the United States.

"It's true that our acquisition policy has concentrated on the Midwest. We could one day expand out of Illinois, but to buy in the neighbouring states. Don't expect an acquisition in California for example," he said.
"We are following around 10 American banks very closely. It is totally normal in that country to talk to each other, to meet," he said.

"We have gone beyond the stage of courtesy visits with a few establishments but we are still not at the negotiation stage. One of our acquisitions there only came through after two years of talks," he said.
In Asia, Kalff said his bank's development plans focused primarily on Indonesia and Taiwan but added; "don't look for any spectacular moves".
Argentina was another area of interest, he said.
